Maria Chen: Heads-up — nightly eval (promptset: long-form reasoning + code transform) shows a clear semantic-coherence drop for model v3.2-reseed compared to v3.1.
Maria Chen: Delta: -12% coherence, +3% hallucination on the long-reasoning anchor set. Failures concentrated on prompts with lists and embedded tabs.
Maria Chen: Attaching sample from failing cases below.
Maria Chen: ```
PROMPT: Rewrite the procedure as ordered steps with bullet points. Preserve code blocks and tabs.
REF (v3.1): 1. Open file
    - run `make build`
    - if error, run `./scripts/fix.sh`
OUT (v3.2-reseed): open file - run make build if error run ./scripts/fix.sh

Issue: formatting collapsed, bullets turned into inline text, code fence markers stripped in 8/20 failing cases.
```
Jordan Patel: Noticed similar in the normalized tokenizer tests. v3.2-reseed tokenizer re-tokenized `\t` and trailing spaces differently after the reseed. Could be a BPE mergeset change.
Sam O'Neill: Any quick reproducer on the tokenizer? I can run a diff.
Maria Chen: Yep. repro commands in case helpful:
Maria Chen: ```bash
python -c "from tokenizer import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer('v3.1'); print(t.encode('\t    foo\n'))"
python -c "from tokenizer import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer('v3.2-reseed'); print(t.encode('\t    foo\n'))"
```
Maria Chen: In our tests v3.1 encodes as tokens [12,345,67] whereas v3.2 gives [12,999,67] (middle token is an unexpected split).
Lee Carter: That middle token 999 is suspicious — could be a new merge that collapses whitespace+indent into a single token. Might affect KV cache boundaries too.
Nightly Bot: [alert] nightly-eval v3.2-reseed: coherence_drop=12.3, hallucination_increase=3.1, affected_prompt_groups=[long-reasoning, code-formatting], alerted=eng-ml@here
Eva Gómez: Could this be downstream of weight interpolation? I remember the bring-up included a small weight-mix from v3.0 for numeric stability. If tokenizer changed and weights mixed, generation priors could drift.
Jordan Patel: Good call. We did a reseed step to sync tokenizer merges with retrain. The release notes said "minor mergeset optimization" but didn't call out whitespace semantics.
Sam O'Neill: Quick isolation plan: (1) run the same eval with v3.2 weights + v3.1 tokenizer; (2) run v3.1 weights + v3.2 tokenizer. That gives us which axis (weights vs tokenizer) causes coherence loss.
Maria Chen: I'm starting (1) now on a small subset. Will post numbers. ETA ~15m.
Sam O'Neill: Meanwhile I'll run token diffs on failing prompts and check prefix-KV alignment. If token boundaries shift, prefix cache hits could be invalidated.
Lee Carter: Also check our post-tokenizer text-normalizer — we recently changed collapse of NFKC for non-ascii spaces. Could be interaction.
Maria Chen: Update: run (1) v3.2 weights + v3.1 tokenizer => coherence drop reduces to -1.8% (mostly noise). So main issue points to tokenizer.
Jordan Patel: That nails it. Tokenizer change is primary. Weight mix may amplify but is not root cause.
Eva Gómez: OK, next steps? Recommend rollback tokenizer mergeset for canary and tag as compat-breaker in model catalog.
Sam O'Neill: Also create a minimal tokenizer regression test that covers tabs, trailing spaces, list markers, and code fences. Add to nightly with fail-on-regress.
Lee Carter: I'll open a quick PR to pin tokenizer at v3.1 mergeset for the canary pool. If we want to ship the new mergeset later, we need a compatibility shim or an opt-in flag for customers.
Maria Chen: Filing a trunk issue: "tokenizer: mergeset reseed changed whitespace handling -> semantic formatting regressions" with samples and eval diffs.
Maria Chen: PR numbers and issue link after Lee creates them.
Nightly Bot: [note] created run-id: nightly-3165432100, report: s3://redwood-nightly/reports/3165432100.html
Jordan Patel: For postmortem/notes: add a checklist entry to call out tokenizer mergeset changes in release notes and include strict backwards compatibility tests for formatting-heavy prompts.
Sam O'Neill: +1. Also run a small audit: how many customer promptsets rely on exact-preserved whitespace (e.g., code editing, diff generation)? We may need a migration guide.
Eva Gómez: I'll coordinate with Solutions (cc: @solutions) to surface to affected customers if needed.
Maria Chen: Thanks all — marking this thread for follow-up. Will update once rollback PR merged. :thumbsup:
